input: Order a DNA ancestry kit as a gift for mom

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Different DNA kits serve different purposes (ancestry breakdown, health reports, relative matching) — knowing what features matter most narrows which kit to buy.
Mom's familiarity with technology and her specific interests (e.g. ethnic origins vs. finding relatives) shapes which product and service tier is the best fit.
Budget determines which brands and tiers are realistic — kits range from ~$50 to $200+ depending on features.
Whether this is for a specific occasion (birthday, holiday, Mother's Day) affects how urgently it needs to arrive and whether gift wrapping or a gift message matters.
Knowing whether to ship directly to mom's address or to the user's address changes the order details and surprise factor.
There are several major brands (AncestryDNA, 23andMe, MyHeritage, etc.) — the user may already have a preference or need guidance on which to choose.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — e.g. a physical kit with a gift note vs. a digital gift card — determines the exact product and presentation to order.

gold.taskTitle: Order a DNA ancestry kit gift for mom
gold.taskDescription: Purchase and arrange delivery of a DNA ancestry testing kit as a gift for the user's mother.

questions.title: Which ancestry features matter most to your mom?
questions.description: Determine whether mom is most interested in ethnic/regional breakdown, health and trait reports, or finding and connecting with DNA relatives — this drives which kit is the right fit.

questions.title: How tech-comfortable is your mom with online platforms?
questions.description: Assess mom's ease with creating accounts and navigating results online, since some services are more beginner-friendly than others.

questions.title: What is your budget for this gift?
questions.description: Establish a price range to filter realistic options, as kits vary from roughly $50 for basic ancestry to $200+ for premium health and ancestry bundles.

questions.title: Is this gift tied to a specific date or occasion?
questions.description: Find out if there is a deadline (birthday, Mother's Day, holiday) to determine how urgently the kit needs to arrive and whether expedited shipping is needed.

questions.title: Should the kit ship directly to your mom or to you?
questions.description: Clarify the delivery address — sending to mom is more convenient but may spoil the surprise, while shipping to the user allows for personal presentation.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred brand already in mind?
questions.description: Check whether the user is leaning toward a specific provider such as AncestryDNA, 23andMe, or MyHeritage, or needs a recommendation based on requirements.

questions.title: Should this be a physical kit box or a digital gift card?
questions.description: Determine the preferred gift format — a physical kit feels more tangible as a present, while a digital gift card lets mom choose her own plan and activate on her own timeline.
